## Logs
Metrics are cheap to add and expensive to keep. Every counter that nobody reads still costs storage, still shows up in the dashboard picker, and still has to be migrated when the backend changes. The rule we settled on is that a metric arrives with the question it answers written next to it, and a metric whose question nobody asks any more is deleted rather than left to rot. ## Sampling of traces
Traces are sampled at the tail, not the head, so a request is kept because it was slow or it failed, not because a coin came up heads when it started. Head sampling throws away exactly the requests worth looking at. The collector buffers spans for thirty seconds before deciding, which is the longest request we are willing to keep in memory.

## Cardinality budget
No label may carry a user id, an email or a request id. Those turn one time series into millions, and the bill arrives a month later. The budget is ten thousand series per service, checked in CI.
